headline_finding: Cross-domain research (via NVIDIA API) confirms: rate-limited actuator control and sensor-health-aware fallback are well-known engineering techniques used in aerospace, robotics, automotive, and industrial automation. The novelty is NOT the mechanisms but their specific APPLICATION to multi-segment hydraulic drainage under physiological sensing constraints. This is an application patent, not a mechanism patent. The mechanism IS generalizable to other distributed-flow-control domains (vascular devices, industrial fluid networks, HVAC, power systems).

P3_cross_domain_research.method: Comprehensive query on rate-limited actuator control and sensor-health-aware fallback across 9 engineering domains
findings: Rate-limited actuator control: ALREADY USED in aerospace (Boeing 787 flight control), robotics (KUKA LBR iiwa), automotive (ESC), power systems (Siemens SIMOTICS), industrial automation (Allen-Bradley PowerFlex)
Sensor-health-aware fallback: ALREADY USED in medical devices (Medtronic ventilator), industrial automation (Rockwell ControlLogix), aerospace (Boeing 737 MAX)
The COMBINATION in a hydraulic drainage context: NOT FOUND in cross-domain search — appears novel as an application
The moat is the APPLICATION, not the mechanism. This is an application patent position.
P3_cross_domain_research.generalizability: The mechanism (bounded rate + sensor-health fallback) is generalizable to ANY domain with distributed flow control, sensor uncertainty, and safety-critical operation. Potential: vascular devices, industrial fluid networks, HVAC, power systems.

P2_ablation.honest_assessment: Ablation runs are compute-bound (each V2 ablation run takes ~6s, 195 remaining runs = ~20 minutes, exceeding session timeouts). Background process unstable. Full ablation deferred. Seed 42 data (30 runs, 9 attacks) confirms rate limiting is universally critical (32-78% of V2 on all 9 attacks).
P2_ablation.what_we_can_say: Rate limiting is strongly implicated as the critical mechanism across seed 42 × 9 attacks.
P2_ablation.what_we_cannot_say: Minimum commercially useful architecture across all seeds and all V2.1 configurations.
